newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbian students celebrate as police lift cordon.
newsitem.headline: Serbian students celebrate as police lift cordon.

text.p: Serbian riot police on Monday lifted a cordon that had blocked student pro-democracy protesters from marching for over a week and let them roam round central Belgrade, witnesses said.

Thousands of students, who have been holding a non-stop rally for more than eight days, marched jubilantly around the city centre, shouting "let's go for a walk" and blowing whistles, the witnesses said.
They said the police withdrew the cordon at about 4 a.m. (0300 GMT).

The move marked a major concession by the Socialist authorities. President Slobodan Milosevic's government has largely ignored demands by the students and the opposition Zajedno (Together) coalition to reinstate annulled local election results last November.

The students, demonstrating 24-hours a day in the bitter cold of the Balkan winter, have kept up their spirits with speeches, dancing to rock music, and by playing stunts such as getting women students to kiss policemen.
The Serbian Orthodox church, siding with the protesters, planned to lead a religious procession through Belgrade later on Monday.

The church, which backed Serbian nationalist war aims during the Yugoslav conflict, stayed silent for weeks while protests swept Serbia's cities to try to force the ruling Socialists to accept defeats in the November municipal elections.
But Patriarch Pavle, who blessed student protesters at a rally last week, said he would lead his flock along Belgrade's Kolarceva Street to St Sava Cathedral starting at 7.30 a.m. (0630 GMT).

Hundreds of thousands of opposition supporters joined a procession led by the patriarch on Orthodox Christmas Eve three weeks ago. Police relaxed an edict against street marches for the occasion and no violence was reported.
Since Thursday the Socialists had loosened the leash on riot police wearied by round-the-clock duty in the winter cold.

The police pummelled protesters, including women and children, blocking roads in several cities. Seven people were injured in an attack on demonstrators sitting on a highway outside the provincial city of Kragujevac.
